title: Semilinear tensor transport through a ring presentation
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in the common sheaf-value universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism, so $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $T=Y,X$ for the two topoi. Let $D_T\to A_T$ and $D_T\to B_T$ be maps of commutative ring sheaves, let $R_T$ be another commutative ring sheaf, and supply ring isomorphisms
$$\beta_T:A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_T\xrightarrow{\sim}R_T.$$
Suppose $d:f^{-1}D_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}D_X$, $a:f^{-1}A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$, $b:f^{-1}B_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X$, and $c:f^{-1}R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X$ are ring isomorphisms. Assume $a,b$ commute with the two $D$-algebra structure maps over $d$, and
$$c f^{-1}\beta_Y=\beta_X(a\otimes b)\sigma_f,$$
where $\sigma_f:f^{-1}(A_Y\otimes_{D_Y}B_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{-1}A_Y\otimes_{f^{-1}D_Y}f^{-1}B_Y$ is the canonical pure-tensor inverse-image comparison.

For $A_T$-module sheaves $M_T$ let $s:f^{-1}M_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}M_X$ be an additive isomorphism semilinear over $a$. Give $N_T=M_T\otimes_{D_T}B_T$ the $R_T$-action transported by $\beta_T$ from
$$(x\otimes b_0)(m\otimes b_1)=xm\otimes b_0b_1.$$
Then there is a unique additive isomorphism
$$r:f^{-1}N_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}N_X$$
whose adjunct is $m\otimes v\mapsto\widetilde s(m)\otimes\widetilde b(v)$, where $\widetilde s:M_Y\to f_*M_X$ and $\widetilde b:B_Y\to f_*B_X$ are the actual adjoints of $s,b$, and the target tensor is mapped into $f_*N_X$ by the sectionwise tensor pairing. It is semilinear over $c$: $r(z n)=c(z)r(n)$ for local sections of $f^{-1}R_Y$ and $f^{-1}N_Y$.

This construction is natural under compatible changes of $B$ and $R$: if $B'_T,R'_T,\beta'_T,b',c'$ satisfy the same assumptions, $q_T:B_T\to B'_T$ are $D_T$-algebra maps, $i_T:R_T\to R'_T$ obey $i_T\beta_T=\beta'_T(1\otimes q_T)$, and $b'f^{-1}q_Y=q_Xb$, $c'f^{-1}i_Y=i_Xc$, then with $j_T=1_{M_T}\otimes q_T$ the resulting maps satisfy
$$r' f^{-1}j_Y=j_Xr.$$
There is no local-freeness, finiteness, completeness, or existence of points hypothesis on these module sheaves or topoi.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-construction] with the given ring isomorphism d and identity structural map to construct an algebraic inverse image I from DY-modules to DX-modules. Its underlying functor is F and its operations satisfy the graph transport equations [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] to obtain the natural tensor comparison, normalized on arbitrary generalized pure tensors. Taking the product sheaf and its projections gives the corresponding equality of pairing morphisms.

Write $\otimes_p$ for the sectionwise presheaf tensor, so that $X\otimes_{D_T}Y$ is the abelian-group sheafification of $X\otimes_pY$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The ring sheaf $A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_T$ of the statement is the ring sheafification of the presheaf of commutative rings $P_T=A_T\otimes_pB_T$, $P_T(U)=A_T(U)\otimes_{D_T(U)}B_T(U)$. For each $U$, $M_T(U)\otimes_{D_T(U)}B_T(U)$ is an ordinary $P_T(U)$-module by $(x\otimes v)(m\otimes w)=xm\otimes vw$: the formula is additive in each variable, and the two balancing checks $(\delta x)m\otimes vw=xm\otimes(\delta v)w$ and $x(\delta m)\otimes vw=xm\otimes v(\delta w)$ are the $D_T(U)$-tensor relation; associativity $(xx')m\otimes(vv')w=x(x'm)\otimes v(v'w)$ and the unit $1m\otimes1w=m\otimes w$ hold on pure inputs. Restrictions preserve the formula, so $M_T\otimes_pB_T$ is a presheaf of $P_T$-modules. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] its abelian sheafification $N_T$ carries a unique map $(A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_T)\times N_T\to N_T$ compatible with this presheaf action, and it is a module action. Pulling it back along $\beta_T^{-1}$ gives exactly the stated $R_T$-action. Below, an action or a linear map is identified by the same lemma: by its uniqueness clause, and by its factorization clause (a $P$-linear presheaf map out of a presheaf module factors uniquely through a $P^\#$-linear map out of its sheafification, whose underlying additive map is the abelian factorization). [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] is used for maps out of a two-factor tensor.

proof.text: Restrict s to DY using da_comm, and regard b as DY-semilinear using db_comm and its multiplicativity. The transported addition and scalar equations turn I(MY) and I(BY) into module isomorphisms with MX and BX: lift their underlying set maps using the operation equations, and reflect isomorphisms through the forgetful functor. Tensor these isomorphisms and compose with the normalized inverse-image tensor comparison to construct r. Its additivity and generalized pure formula follow from the same properties of these module maps.

The adjunction hom equivalence identifies the required adjunct formula with the equality of pure-pairing morphisms already proved. Unit naturality and preservation of binary products by the actual right adjoint show that the mate of the product of two maps is their two mates followed by the inverse product comparison. Thus the normalization is for the supplied adjunction, with no additional adjoint chosen.

Prove that additive morphisms out of a sheaf tensor are determined on pure tensors: compose with its abelian sheafification presentation, use the abelian sheafification adjunction, and induct on ordinary tensors. For morphisms out of F of the tensor, lift additive graphs through I to abelian sheaf maps, then precompose with the inverse-image pure pairing. That pairing factors through an isomorphism from the tensor of the image modules. Apply the preceding additive extensionality result. Consequently two additive isomorphisms with the adjunct formula agree. Use [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-pure-pairing] for that map and [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-pairing-isIso] for its invertibility.

Equip NY with the RY-action constructed in step 2, obtaining an actual RY-module sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-construction] to the ring isomorphism c to transport this module to RX. The additive graph of r yields an isomorphism of its underlying abelian sheaf with NX. Transport its sectionwise module structures through this additive isomorphism. Naturality of the isomorphism proves restriction compatibility of the resulting action hX; the operation comparison of the geometric module transport proves c-semilinearity of r by construction.

Check the target pure-action formula on the source test sheaf T=(AY times BY) times (MY times BY). Apply the c-semilinearity just established to the source pure-action equation on T. The normalized pairing formula for r identifies its two module terms. The a-semilinearity of s and multiplicativity of b identify the remaining module and coefficient factors. Multiplicativity of c and iA_comm and iB_comm identify the scalar factor. For arbitrary target sections x,v,m,w, invert a,b,s and use the finite-product comparisons to obtain a section of F(T) with precisely these components. Evaluating the transported equation there gives the target pure-action formula. Hence hX is IsTensorAction and r is the required semilinear isomorphism; no global pure-generation claim is needed.

proof.text: Tensor the identity of the restricted module with the D-linear coefficient map q, then forget to abelian sheaves. The pure-map formula gives jY and jX. The two composites in the naturality square are additive. After precomposing with F of the full pure pairing, their formulas agree by the b compatibility equation, functoriality, and the two product projections. Apply the additive extensionality argument of step 5. This proves naturality for every additive primed isomorphism with the given adjunct formula; scalar compatibility assumptions remain available but no additional use of them is needed.
